name: DeepRepoQA
status_reason: Public implementation depends on an unavailable PyArmor native runtime (the obfuscated modules' own required .pyd/.so is absent from the published repository -- confirmed via direct ModuleNotFoundError, not assumed) plus an unavailable VOYAGE_API_KEY. Cannot currently be reproduced faithfully -- there is no source available to patch (unlike HiFiRepoQA), and reimplementing the obfuscated MCTS/selector/value-function logic from the paper's own text would not be a faithful port of the released method, so this has not been attempted and will not be. All integration work (wrapper, manifest, fidelity findings) is preserved as-is. Do not attempt to 'fix' or reimplement this from the paper.
role: external baseline method (repository-domain, MCTS-based deep agent exploration)
commit_note: Pinned this session via live clone (previously 'TO BE PINNED AT CHECKOUT TIME'). Latest commit at clone time: 'Add scripts for the new baseline and the new experiments.'
paper: arXiv:2608.24221, 'DeepRepoQA: Code Repository Question Answering with Deep Agent Exploration' (Weihan Peng et al.), preprint as of audit time; OpenReview forum id k3R9Dq1N6P exists (review venue/outcome unconfirmed)
evaluated_by_authors_on: SWE-QA (arXiv:2509.14635, ACL 2026 Findings, 15 repos) -- CRITICAL: this is a DIFFERENT benchmark from our own SWE-QA-Pro (arXiv:2603.16124, TIGER-AI-Lab, 26 repos). Never evaluated by the authors on SWE-QA-Pro or RepoProbe. Any DeepRepoQA number cited in our paper MUST be labeled as a SWE-QA result, never silently presented as SWE-QA-Pro.
MAJOR_FINDING_this_session: The overwhelming majority of DeepRepoQA's actual method logic in the PUBLISHED repository is PyArmor-obfuscated (compiled/encrypted bytecode, NOT readable or portable Python source) -- discovered by direct inspection, not assumed. Measured file-by-file: DeepRepoQA/actions/ (the 6 custom tools -- FindClass/FindFunction/FindCodeSnippet/FindCalledObject/SemanticSearch/ViewCode) 14/15 files obfuscated; DeepRepoQA/selector/ (the MCTS/UCT selection logic) 4/5 obfuscated; DeepRepoQA/index/ 8/9 obfuscated; DeepRepoQA/value_function/ (the Evaluation Agent's scalar utility scoring) 3/5 obfuscated; DeepRepoQA/feedback/ 3/4 obfuscated; DeepRepoQA/agent/ (CodeQAAgent itself, its prompts, its settings) 4/4 obfuscated -- ALL of it. Only generic infrastructure is open: DeepRepoQA/codeblocks/, DeepRepoQA/completion/ (the LLM client wrapper), DeepRepoQA/repository/ (repo abstraction) are 0% obfuscated, plus the top-level example.py/example_batch.py calling scripts. CONSEQUENCE: this session's (and any prior pass's) algorithmic description of DeepRepoQA's MCTS/UCT formula, its tool implementations, and its value-function scoring was necessarily sourced from the PAPER's own text, not verified against the actual released code -- the actual released code cannot be read, verified, or faithfully ported at the method-logic level in this environment, only invoked as a sealed black box through its open calling interface (example.py's initialize_qa_system()/ask_question() functions).
BLOCKING_execution_status: CONFIRMED NOT RUNNABLE in this environment -- three independent, verified blockers, any one of which alone is sufficient to block Stage 3:
blocker_1_pyarmor_runtime_missing: The obfuscated modules import a `pyarmor_runtime_000000` package whose OWN native runtime binary (a compiled .pyd/.so PyArmor depends on to decrypt/execute the obfuscated bytecode) is NOT present anywhere in the published repository -- only an __init__.py stub exists in DeepRepoQA/pyarmor_runtime_000000/ and DeepRepoQA/agent/pyarmor_runtime_000000/, no compiled extension. Verified live: `from DeepRepoQA.agent.code_qa_agent import CodeQAAgent` raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pyarmor_runtime_000000'` immediately. This is a structural gap in what the authors published, not an environment misconfiguration -- unfixable without the authors publishing the missing runtime file (or a fresh PyArmor license/rebuild of their own). Also worth flagging: the obfuscation header reads 'Pyarmor 9.1.9 (trial)' -- a TRIAL license, which commonly carries its own expiration/machine-binding/watermarking restrictions even when the runtime IS present; this was not able to be further characterized since the runtime itself is absent.
blocker_2_python_version: environment.yml pins Python 3.11 (cpython=3.11.13) via conda, with many conda-specific package builds -- a plain pip/venv reconstruction would need care. (A system Python 3.11.9 happened to be available in this session's environment, so this alone would not have been a hard blocker -- listed for completeness, since it compounds with blocker_1: PyArmor-compiled bytecode is also typically tied to a specific Python minor version, so even a correctly-versioned interpreter does not by itself guarantee the missing runtime would work if it existed.)
blocker_3_voyage_api_key: SemanticSearch (one of the 6 core tools) requires the voyage-code-3 embedding model via a paid Voyage AI API key. VOYAGE_API_KEY is not configured in this environment (confirmed: unset, and the checkout's own bundled .env template ships it empty). Per this suite's own fairness design (see external_wrappers/deeprepoqa.py's existing docstring), this must fail loudly rather than silently substitute a different embedder, which would make any resulting comparison SEMI-CONTROLLED at best without disclosure.

roles: Execution Agent (executes actions via repo index)
Evaluation Agent (scalar utility scoring + qualitative guidance)
agent_architecture.search_mechanism: Genuine MCTS per the PAPER's own text: UCT selection Q(s,a) + c*sqrt(ln N(s)/N(s,a)), max 3 children/node expansion, max 15 iterations, temperature 0.7 exploration / 0 generation -- NOT independently verifiable against the actual released selector code in this environment (see MAJOR_FINDING above: DeepRepoQA/selector/ is 4/5 obfuscated).
tools: FindCalledObject (present in example.py's own import list, not mentioned in the paper's own tool enumeration -- a real discrepancy between the paper text and the actual calling code, itself only visible because example.py is unobfuscated)

proprietary_dependency: voyage-code-3 embedding model (Voyage AI, paid API) for SemanticSearch -- see blocker_3 above.
model_assumptions: Model-agnostic (prompted inference only, no training) -- evaluated by authors across GLM-4.6, Kimi K2, Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct, GPT-5.1. example.py's own CompletionModel reads CUSTOM_LLM_MODEL/CUSTOM_LLM_API_BASE/CUSTOM_LLM_API_KEY from .env -- this part of the calling code IS open and would accept gpt-4.1 against api.openai.com without any code change, moot given blockers 1 and 3.
gpt_4_1_substitution: Mechanically trivial at the CALLING-CODE level (CompletionModel's own env-var-driven config, unobfuscated) -- but cannot be verified to actually reach the obfuscated CodeQAAgent/selector/value_function internals in this environment (blocker_1).
compute_overhead_vs_single_pass: Real and non-trivial per the paper's own text: up to 15 MCTS iterations x up to 3-way expansion x a 4-role Perception/Planning/Execution/Evaluation loop per node is substantially more LLM calls than a single ReAct pass -- NOT independently measurable in this environment since the method cannot currently be run at all.
porting_effort_to_sweqa_pro_or_repoprobe: Cannot be meaningfully assessed beyond the calling-script level (example.py's repo_path/question inputs, which are already benchmark-agnostic) until blocker_1 is resolved -- there is no method-logic porting question to answer when the method's own logic is inaccessible.
environment_strategy: Pinned external checkout under third_party/checkouts/deeprepoqa (gitignored, never committed to ANT's own repo). NO local modifications attempted or made -- unlike HiFiRepoQA, there is no code available to patch (the blocking component is a missing binary, not a bug in readable source).
execution_status: NOT executed -- confirmed not runnable via direct verification (blocker_1's ModuleNotFoundError reproduced live), not merely assumed from missing credentials. See external_wrappers/deeprepoqa.py for the wrapper's own design (unchanged this session, since there is nothing new to wire up while blocker_1 stands).
local_modifications: None -- none possible without the missing PyArmor runtime, which this suite has no way to obtain or reconstruct.
recommendation: Do not budget DeepRepoQA into any near-term formal run. Resolving this would require the authors publishing the missing pyarmor_runtime binary (or an unobfuscated release), which is outside this project's control -- flag to the paper's authors directly if contact is established, or treat DeepRepoQA as EXTERNAL-PUBLISHED-REFERENCE-ONLY (their own SWE-QA numbers, clearly labeled as a different benchmark) rather than a reproduced/controlled baseline in this suite.
